newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian paras to face trial over Somalia charges.
newsitem.headline: Belgian paras to face trial over Somalia charges.

text.p: Three Belgian paratroopers who served in a multinational peacekeeping force in Somalia in 1993 will face a military court on Monday on charges they physically abused Somali youths while on duty.

If found guilty on the charges of threatening behaviour and physical violence they could be sent to prison, a military court official told Reuters on Friday. He gave no indication of the term they could be sentenced to.

The case came to light after the paper Het Laatste Nieuws published photographs earlier this year of soldiers holding a youth over an open fire, forcing others to eat worms and other acts described by Belgian Defence Minister Jean-Pol Poncelet as horrible and tasteless.
The allegations sparked a review of paratroop training and caused Poncelet to wonder in public whether the third paratroop batallion the men belonged to should be scrapped.

The charges against the three Belgians mirror those made separately against members of Canadian and Italian forces who also served with United Nations forces in Somalia. Around 1,000 Belgian troops took part in operation "Restore Hope".
